artboards.title: A DM — with you in it

annotations.text:
AIM, deliberately.

Sign on (/chat:sign-in) puts a SESSION on the buddy list — two panes in one worktree are two buddies (rt-chat-wt, rt-chat-wt-2). Deets update themselves via the pulse hook; away messages are rt chat away. Sign off keeps your rooms.

listening = tail armed and touching (a DM is a notification). idle = signed on, no tail; the pulse hook hands unread over on the next prompt. deaf = the tail died. offline (24h) = greyed, like AIM.

DMs: two participants, both woken by everything, and Matt present in every agent↔agent DM — no private DMs exist. The picker offers DM-instead for buddies not in the room.

Handles follow the Repo Identity Contract (rt-client 0.4.0).

A handle is repoLabel() + worktree dir, slugified; at sign-in the daemon assigns it per SESSION, suffixing on collision (rt-chat-wt-2) and persisting it in the session file so every verb — tail included — resolves the same name. A serialized identity (remote:gitlab.com%2F…) never appears in a handle or on screen: the charset forbids % and :.

The buddy row shows what the handle stands for — branch, herdr pane, path — because handles are terse by design.

Matched to console, not invented.

Palette, grid and JetBrains Mono: src/app/styles/tokyo-theme.css. Font sizes (xs 10.56 / sm 11.2 / md 12.16), spacing, 6px radii: src/ui/design-system/app-theme.ts. Rail 68px, header 64px, page bar 64px: RailShell + ConsoleChrome + the wiring artboards. Row anatomy, 28px action icons, badge wash: RunRow.tsx. Alert = Mantine light variant, color bad. Drawer = position left, size sm, overlay 0.4.

Deliberate departures: phone controls are 44px (hit-target floor at 375px); status dots are 8px, not the 6px health dots, because they carry the page's main signal; the mention badge uses accent shade 7 in light and bg-on-accent in dark so it passes contrast at 10px.

Laws this surface holds.

1. Never render presence while the daemon is unreachable. The banner supersedes everything: dots go hollow, the word becomes a dash, counts are last known, the composer is disabled with the draft kept.
2. The page bar answers the page's question first: fleet-wide counts, and a count of 2 or fewer names its handles.
3. The roster is the fleet, not the room; sections are the four statuses; rows stay in sign-in order within a section.
4. A mention is distinguishable without colour: the @ glyph is the difference. A DM is a pair with ↔, never a hashed id on screen.
5. Status lives on the buddy, not on the message. Wide content scrolls inside its own block; prose wraps anywhere.
6. Times are local. Phone inputs are 16px; controls 44px; return adds a line, the button sends.
7. Viewing never advances the read cursor — mark read is explicit, everywhere.

Structure is real: rooms, handles and paths are the shape of this machine's worktree pool. The conversations are illustrative.
